speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly how the swelling and pain started, and have you noticed any recent injuries or bites to that finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury suggests a possible mallet finger or joint sprain. Can you actively extend the tip of your right ring finger fully against resistance, or does it lag behind?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to actively extend the fingertip combined with the injury mechanism strongly suggests a mallet finger injury involving the extensor tendon. I need to confirm if there is a bony fragment or significant joint involvement. REQUEST TEST: Right Ring Finger X-Ray

text: The X-ray rules out a bony avulsion fracture, so this is likely a pure tendinous mallet finger injury. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out any associated flexor tendon injury, are you able to actively flex the tip of your finger (make a hook fist), and do you have any numbness in the fingertip?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming your medical history. I have sufficient clinical evidence to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger
